text.p: LME copper took a breath on Tuesday afternoon, looking for a comfortable lower level, while lead slumped to a fresh 18-month nadir and was vulnerable to more losses, traders said. All of the other metals ended the day softer except aluminium, which kept up a robust performance.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau index added 0.44 points to 246.68.

Three months LME copper ended the afternoon kerb little changed after testing both sides of the market, drifting to $2,346 per tonne in the morning and climbing to $2,374 after lunch. Last business was $4 up at $2,360.
Lead spiralled lower after breaching the bottom of its recent range, ending $15 lower at $615, the lowest level since October 12, 1995. Support was pegged at $610/15, $600, and $580.
Aluminium shook off the weakness in the others and continued to forge higher, ending the day $9 firmer at $1,637.50.
Zinc ended barely changed, down $3 at $1,264, after trading between $1,272 and $1,261. The market will be eyeing stocks data for signs of Chinese material heading for Singapore.

Nickel fared less well, ending the day well below the 10-day moving average at $7,280 with a $180 loss. Any further falls should find good support at $7,110, which put a floor on the downside on April 14 and January 29.
Tin was also looking shaky, ending the kerb $65 weaker at its low of $5,650, down $65. The market was in danger of retesting its April 11 low of $5,600, analysts said.

CBOT wheat futures closed mostly higher on a technical bounce tied to signals the market was oversold after the recent price break, traders said. Wheat closed two cents higher to two lower, with May down one at $4.11 and July was up 1-3/4 at $4.23.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended slightly higher Tuesday, helped by sharply higher U.S. bond prices and a weaker U.S. dollar, after U.S. economic data suggested the Federal Reserve may not raise interest rates again in May. COMEX June gold ended up 20 cents at $341.60 an ounce, after trading a $340.80-342.20 range. Estimated total volume in COMEX gold was moderate at 19,000 lots. In the bullion market spot gold ended quoted $339.70/20, after fixing in London Tuesday afternoon at $339.25. Earlier spot gold had fixed Tuesday morning at $338.95, the lowest since February 12 this year when four year lows were seen.

NYMEX heating oil rallied Tuesday, sending oil prices surging, as heating oil's May contract expiry approached amid tight supplies, triggering short covering. "There was a lot of talk of a short squeeze because someone may be taking a large delivery," said Nauman Barakat, trader with Prudential Securities, of the heating oil rally. May heating oil ended up 2.38 cents a gallon at 58.91 cents. June crude finished up 53 cents at $20.44 a barrel while May gasoline ended up 1.02 cents a gallon at 63.36 cents.
